What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
Electropolished pipe and fittings are precision-finished stainless steel products designed for applications where cleanliness, corrosion resistance and surface smoothness are critical. During electropolishing, a controlled electrochemical process removes microscopic surface irregularities, producing a bright, passive and contamination-resistant finish. These products are widely used in pharmaceutical manufacturing, biotechnology, food processing, dairy plants, semiconductor facilities and high-purity process systems.

Sakshi Forge supplies electropolished pipes and fittings in SS304L and SS316L grades with consistent internal surface finish, dimensional accuracy and complete material traceability. Products are available in various sizes, schedules and end connections including butt weld, tri-clamp and orbital welding compatible designs. Every product undergoes strict quality inspection to ensure compliance with international standards and demanding industrial environments.

FAQs.q: What are the specifications of SS 321 Seamless Pipe?
FAQs.a: Available in UNS S32100 (ASTM A312 TP321), OD 1/8"–24" NB, Sch 5S–160, hot finished or cold drawn seamless construction, titanium-stabilized at 5xC minimum.

FAQs.q: Why is SS 321 preferred over 304L for high temperature welded service?
FAQs.a: 321's titanium stabilization prevents sensitization at temperatures above 425°C where 304L can still be susceptible to intergranular corrosion, since 304L only manages carbon during/immediately after welding, not during subsequent hot service.

FAQs.q: Is 321 recommended for continuous service above 550°C?
FAQs.a: Extended exposure can lead to "knife-line attack" adjacent to welds in some conditions; for the most demanding, prolonged high-temperature service, 347 (niobium-stabilized) is sometimes preferred as an alternative.

FAQs.q: Does 321 offer better strength than 304H at high temperature?
FAQs.a: Their high-temperature allowable stresses are broadly comparable under ASME Section II; the choice between them is usually driven by welding/fabrication sequence and specific project specification rather than raw strength.

FAQs.q: Does Sakshi Forge provide Material Test Certificates (MTC) for SS 321 Seamless Pipe?
FAQs.a: Yes, MTC as per EN 10204 3.1 is provided with every dispatch along with inspection reports.

What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
SS 321 (UNS S32100 / ASTM A312 TP321) is a titanium-stabilized austenitic stainless steel pipe specifically engineered for continuous service in the elevated temperature sensitization range of 425°C to 850°C (800°F to 1500°F). The addition of titanium (dosed at a minimum of 5 times carbon content) preferentially binds carbon to form stable titanium carbides during mill heat treatment. This prevents chromium carbide precipitation at grain boundaries during welding or high-temperature exposure, thereby eliminating intergranular corrosion (sensitization) and preserving full corrosion resistance in post-weld elevated-temperature environments.

Sakshi Forge manufactures SS 321 seamless pipes using hot extrusion and precision cold drawing, followed by a stabilizing anneal. These pipes feature a smooth, seamless bore, superior creep-rupture strength, and excellent scaling resistance. They are widely specified across thermal power plants, petroleum refining units, chemical process lines, aircraft exhaust collectors, and boiler superheaters where standard 304/304L stainless steels cannot provide long-term high-temperature reliability.

What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
SS 347 (UNS S34700 / ASTM A312 TP347) is a niobium (columbium) stabilized austenitic stainless steel seamless pipe engineered for severe high-temperature service up to 850°C (1560°F). Niobium is added at a minimum of 10 times the carbon content (up to 1.00% max) to form ultra-stable niobium carbides (NbC). These carbides prevent chromium carbide precipitation at grain boundaries during thermal exposure, providing exceptional protection against intergranular corrosion.

Compared to titanium-stabilized SS 321, niobium in SS 347 has a lower affinity for oxidation during electric-arc and TIG welding. This delivers superior weld pool fluidity, enhanced multi-pass weld integrity, and better creep-rupture strength retention in heavy-wall piping sections. Sakshi Forge manufactures SS 347 seamless pipes per ASTM A312 and ASME SA312 standards, supplied fully solution annealed and pickled with 100% NDT inspection for power generation steam systems, petroleum hydroprocessing, and chemical reactors.

SS 904L (UNS N08904 / ASTM A312 TP904L) is a high-alloy super-austenitic stainless steel seamless pipe engineered for extreme resistance to sulfuric, phosphoric, and organic acids across a broad range of temperatures and concentrations. Its chemistry features high nickel (23.0%–28.0%), high chromium (19.0%–23.0%), molybdenum (4.0%–5.0%), and a deliberate copper addition (1.0%–2.0%). Sakshi Forge supplies fully solution-annealed and passivated SS 904L seamless pipes for fertilizer plants, flue-gas desulfurization (FGD) scrubbers, chemical processing reactors, and seawater piping.

It is the gold standard material for seawater desalination plants, subsea oil & gas piping, bleach plant pulp washing, and flue-gas desulfurization absorbers.

What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
Duplex 2205 (UNS S32205 / S31803 / EN 1.4462) is the workhorse dual-phase stainless steel seamless pipe, engineered with a balanced ~50% ferrite and ~50% austenite microstructure. Its chemistry comprises 22.0%–23.0% Chromium, 4.5%–6.5% Nickel, 3.0%–3.5% Molybdenum, and 0.14%–0.20% Nitrogen, yielding a Pitting Resistance Equivalent Number (PREN) > 35.

This dual-phase structure delivers approximately double the yield strength (≥450 MPa) of standard 316L (220 MPa) in the solution-annealed condition, allowing engineers to significantly reduce wall thickness and pipe weight for equivalent pressure ratings under ASME B31.3. Furthermore, the ferrite phase imparts virtual immunity to chloride stress corrosion cracking (SCC). Sakshi Forge manufactures Duplex 2205 seamless pipes via hot extrusion and cold drawing, followed by rapid water quenching from 1020–1100°C to lock in phase balance and prevent embrittling sigma phase precipitation.

Duplex 2304 (UNS S32304 / EN 1.4362) is a lean-alloyed dual-phase stainless steel seamless pipe engineered as a high-strength, cost-effective alternative to standard 304L and 316L austenitic stainless steels. It omits the intentional molybdenum addition found in 2205 (carrying only trace Mo ≤ 0.60%) while maintaining a 23% Chromium and 4% Nickel dual-phase austenite-ferrite structure stabilized by nitrogen (0.05%–0.20%).

This lean composition delivers double the yield strength (≥400 MPa) of 316L alongside general corrosion resistance and PREN (~25) comparable to 316L. By minimizing expensive nickel and molybdenum additions, Duplex 2304 reduces raw material cost and market price volatility. Sakshi Forge manufactures Duplex 2304 seamless pipes via hot extrusion and cold drawing, followed by solution annealing. It is widely specified for storage tank piping, structural marine frames, pulp digesters, and moderate-corrosion industrial process lines.

What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
15-5 PH (UNS S15500 / XM-12 / EN 1.4545) is a delta-ferrite-free martensitic precipitation-hardening stainless steel seamless pipe engineered to overcome the transverse directional toughness limitations of standard 17-4 PH. Its chemistry is tightly controlled to 14.0%–15.5% Chromium, 3.5%–5.5% Nickel, 2.5%–4.5% Copper, and 0.15%–0.45% Niobium. Rebalancing the chromium and nickel ratios completely eliminates delta-ferrite from the microstructure.

This ferrite-free structure imparts exceptional short-transverse impact toughness, crack propagation resistance, and uniform multi-directional mechanical properties. Like 17-4 PH, 15-5 PH achieves ultra-high yield strengths (up to 1170 MPa / 170 ksi) via a simple low-temperature aging heat treatment (H900 to H1150). Sakshi Forge manufactures 15-5 PH seamless pipes per AMS 5659 and ASTM A564 standards, processed via ESR (Electro-Slag Remelting) or VAR (Vacuum Arc Remelting) for extreme cleanliness. It is widely specified for critical aerospace structural piping, aircraft hydraulic control lines, nuclear components, and high-pressure defense applications.

What Is This Product? (150-200 words):
13-8 Mo (UNS S13800 / PH 13-8 Mo / EN 1.4534) is an ultra-high-strength, premium double-vacuum melted (VIM/VAR) martensitic precipitation-hardening stainless steel seamless pipe. Engineered for the most demanding aerospace, defense, and subsea structural applications, its chemistry consists of 12.25%–13.25% Chromium, 7.5%–8.5% Nickel, 2.0%–2.5% Molybdenum, and 0.90%–1.35% Aluminum.

Through VIM (Vacuum Induction Melting) followed by VAR (Vacuum Arc Remelting), 13-8 Mo achieves extraordinary micro-structural cleanliness, eliminating harmful inclusions and directional weaknesses. Low-temperature age hardening (precipitating B2 NiAl intermetallic particles) yields tensile strengths up to 1450 MPa (210 ksi) and yield strengths up to 1350 MPa (195 ksi), combined with superior fracture toughness and outstanding resistance to stress corrosion cracking (SCC). Sakshi Forge manufactures 13-8 Mo seamless pipes per AMS 5629 and ASTM A564 standards, supplied Condition A or pre-aged (H950, H1000, H1050, H1100, H1150) for critical aerospace landing gear hydraulics, missile structures, and subsea shafting.
